ambiguities.aspect: enable synchronizer depth / whether en_data_reg counts as one of the two flops
readings: en_data_reg (clk_a) + en_clap_one + en_clap_two (clk_b) = 3 flops total, so dataout updates 2 clk_b edges after en_data_reg rises (as literally listed in the register description)

the 'two D flip-flops' are the entire delay chain from data_en (data_en sampled directly by clk_b into en_clap_one), so dataout updates 2 clk_b edges after data_en, i.e. one clk_b cycle earlier than the first reading
dataout is loaded directly from data_reg (a clk_a flop) on the same clk_b edge that en_clap_two is high, adding zero extra latency (as written in 'Output Assignment')
data_reg must itself be re-registered through two clk_b flops before being selected, so dataout appears 2 clk_b cycles later and a different (already-stable) value is captured
data_reg is updated with data_in on every clk_a edge regardless of data_en, so it can already hold the next value when the synchronized enable arrives
data_reg is only updated while data_en is high (enable-qualified capture), so it holds the value present during the enable window

ambiguities.aspect: level-sensitive vs one-shot (edge) use of en_clap_two
readings: dataout reloads data_reg on every clk_b edge while en_clap_two is high (level-sensitive mux), so any change of data_reg during a long enable window propagates to dataout
en_clap_two is treated as a single-cycle pulse/edge detect, so dataout is loaded exactly once per data_en event and never follows data_reg afterwards
